tools.name: check_route

params.name: from_place
params.doc: Start of the drive: a city, town or landmark name.

params.name: to_place
params.doc: End of the drive.

params.name: from_coords
params.doc: Start as "lat,lon". Pass it whenever you know it: it lets small towns and landmarks resolve, and it clips the corridor to the stretch actually driven.

params.name: to_coords
params.doc: End as "lat,lon". Same rules as from_coords.

tools.title: Check a route
tools.summary: Everything active along one of 17 curated California corridors, ordered by miles from the start, with a summary.
tools.reads: CHP incidents, Caltrans lane closures in place, chain controls, wildfires within about 10 miles, plus weather, road-weather stations, recent earthquakes, signs and cameras along the way.
tools.refresh: Incidents about once a minute; closures, chains and fires on a five-minute cache.
tools.caps: Not a general router. When no corridor matches, the response lists the covered corridors; use the filtered tools with center for anything else.

tools.name: check_region

params.name: region
params.doc: One of: Bay Area, Sacramento metro, Tahoe/Sierra, Central Valley, Southern California, San Diego, Central Coast, North State. Any other value returns the list.

tools.title: Check a region
tools.summary: One-call report for a whole region: exact counts, incidents severity first, full closures called out, chain controls, fires.
tools.reads: Every California source over the region at once.
tools.refresh: Incidents about once a minute; the rest on a five-minute cache.
tools.caps: Large regions cap each list to the most severe items. Counts are always exact and the response says when a list was truncated.

tools.name: get_incidents

params.name: highway
params.doc: A route as people write it: "I-80", "US 50", "17", "Hwy 99". Matches incidents whose location text names that route.

params.name: area
params.doc: Substring of a CHP dispatch-area name ("Golden Gate", "East Sac"). These are communication-center names, not towns; for a town use center.

params.name: center
params.doc: "lat,lon". With radius_km, incidents inside that circle. The right filter for a town or place.

params.name: radius_km
params.doc: Radius around center in kilometers. 15 to 30 covers a town.

tools.title: Live incidents
tools.summary: CHP dispatch incidents statewide: collisions, hazards, disabled vehicles, closures as CHP logs them.
tools.reads: The California Highway Patrol computer-aided dispatch feed, fetched live on every call.
tools.refresh: About once a minute; an incident disappears when CHP closes the log.
tools.caps: Locations are dispatcher free text; a few incidents lack usable coordinates and are omitted. Current logs only, no history.

tools.name: get_lane_closures

params.name: district
params.doc: Caltrans district, 1 to 12 (3 Sacramento and Tahoe, 4 Bay Area, 7 Los Angeles).

params.name: center
params.doc: "lat,lon". Closures whose begin or end point is inside the circle.

params.name: radius_km
params.doc: Radius around center in kilometers.

tools.title: Lane closures
tools.summary: Caltrans closures physically in place right now, classified by what they mean for through traffic.
tools.reads: The Caltrans Lane Closure System. Only closures crews have established (CHP code 1097) and not yet picked up; scheduled work that has not started is excluded, and shoulder-only work too.
tools.refresh: Five-minute cache over the per-district feeds.
tools.caps: At most 200 closures per call; total and truncated say when there were more. Read closure_class: full-roadway is the only class that means you cannot drive through.

tools.name: get_chain_controls

params.name: route
params.doc: A mountain route: "80", "US-50", "SR-88".

params.name: center
params.doc: "lat,lon" for every checkpoint around a place, whatever highway.

params.name: radius_km
params.doc: Radius around center in kilometers.

tools.title: Chain controls
tools.summary: Current chain requirements at Caltrans checkpoints on mountain routes.
tools.reads: Caltrans chain-control status. R-1: chains or snow tires. R-2: chains except 4WD/AWD with snow tires. R-3: chains on every vehicle.
tools.refresh: Five-minute cache. Requirements change hour to hour in storms.
tools.caps: Off season (roughly May to October) the response says no controls are active instead of returning an empty list.

tools.name: get_wildfires

params.name: near_route
params.doc: Only fires within about 10 miles of that highway's corridor ("I-5", "101").

params.name: center
params.doc: "lat,lon" for fires around a place, regardless of highway.

params.name: radius_km
params.doc: Radius around center in kilometers.

tools.title: Wildfires
tools.summary: Active California fires with size, containment and the major highways within about 10 miles.
tools.reads: The interagency WFIGS current-wildfire feed. Points are each fire's origin, not its perimeter.
tools.refresh: Five-minute cache; size and containment update once or twice a day.
tools.caps: Knows nothing about road closures caused by a fire; cross-check incidents and lane closures for the area.

tools.name: rank_routes

params.name: by
params.doc: "activity" (live events: full closures weigh most, then incidents, lane closures, chain controls) or "congestion" (measured speed against free flow at each corridor's midpoint; falls back to activity when the traffic feed is off).

params.name: limit
params.doc: How many corridors to return. Default 5, of 17.

tools.title: Rank busiest routes
tools.summary: All 17 corridors ranked by live events or measured congestion, each with counts and a one-line reason.
tools.reads: The same events as check_route, across every corridor.
tools.caps: Congestion ranking needs the traffic feed; without it the ranking silently falls back to activity.

tools.name: get_cameras

params.name: center
params.doc: "lat,lon". Required unless route is given. Results sort nearest first.

params.name: route
params.doc: Narrow to one highway: "I-80", "50".

params.name: radius_km
params.doc: Radius around center in kilometers.

params.name: limit
params.doc: At most 10 verified cameras per call.

tools.title: Highway cameras
tools.summary: Roadside camera snapshots near a point or along a route, each verified live before it is returned.
tools.reads: About 3,000 in-service Caltrans cameras. Offline cameras that serve a placeholder frame are filtered by image freshness.
tools.refresh: Snapshots about once a minute; stream_url, when present, is HLS.
tools.caps: At most 10 cameras per call. center is required unless route is given.

tools.name: get_road_signs

params.name: route
params.doc: A route: "I-80".

params.name: center
params.doc: "lat,lon" with radius_km.

params.name: radius_km
params.doc: Radius around center in kilometers.

tools.title: Message signs
tools.summary: What changeable message signs are displaying right now, verbatim.
tools.reads: Statewide Caltrans CMS text, blank and out-of-service signs already filtered.
tools.caps: Quote sign text verbatim; it is the most current and most local signal there is.

tools.name: get_nearby_events

params.name: center
params.doc: "lat,lon". Required.

params.name: radius_km
params.doc: Radius in kilometers, capped at 160.

params.name: kinds
params.doc: Comma list from incident, closure, chain, fire, sign, rwis, camera, toll. Omit for everything.

tools.title: Nearby events, nationwide
tools.summary: Live road events near a point across every covered state, including California.
tools.reads: State DOT incidents, roadwork and closures, chain and traction advisories, nationwide wildfires, signs, road weather, cameras and toll prices where agencies publish them. Each event names its publishing agency.
tools.refresh: Per source; each response lists every source with its data_as_of.
tools.caps: radius_km caps at 160. Coverage varies by state; the data-sources page has the matrix. For California, the dedicated tools carry more detail.
